solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Nice country song from Israel — a smile breaks out

indicators.note: breaks out suggests the letters burst free and reform in a new order

explanation.surface: A tune from Israel makes someone grin broadly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nice' looks like the adjective but is the French city, so 'Nice country song' is France's national anthem. The anagram signal 'breaks out' works on ISRAEL A SMILE.
explanation.definitionFit: La Marseillaise is the national anthem of France, the country Nice belongs to.

clue.text: Food that millions consume with pride, oddly

parts.note: M is the standard abbreviation for million(s)
to consume food is to eat it

indicators.note: oddly asks for the first, third and fifth letters of the word pride

explanation.surface: Millions proudly tuck into some dish.
explanation.definitionFit: A meat pie is a savoury pastry dish, an example of food.

clue.text: Animal eggs rumoured to be expensive

parts.note: roe is the mass of eggs in a fish

indicators.note: rumoured signals that the word is heard rather than read, giving a sound-alike

parts.note: dear means expensive

explanation.surface: Gossip says caviar costs a lot.
explanation.definitionFit: The roe deer is a small European deer, an example of an animal.

clue.text: List people finishing with some ability at maths

indicators.note: finishing points to the final letter of the word people

parts.note: numerate means competent with numbers

explanation.surface: Name the people who end up decent at arithmetic.
explanation.definitionFit: To enumerate is to name items one by one, which is to list them.

clue.text: Prisoner's right to support existence

indicators.note: in a down clue the supporting letter sits underneath, so it comes after

parts.note: life is existence

explanation.surface: An inmate's right to live is upheld.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Prisoner's' is read as 'Prisoner is', the 's joining definition to wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A lifer is slang for a prisoner serving a life sentence.

clue.text: Gets to a point to cross rolling river

indicators.note: to cross means A and S straddle the other letters

parts.note: S (south) is a compass point

indicators.note: rolling suggests the letters of river tumble into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone reaches a spot where they must ford a swirling river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'point' looks like a place to reach but is a compass point; 'to cross' has A and S straddle the jumbled river, which 'rolling' churns.
explanation.definitionFit: Arrives is a synonym for gets to, reaching a destination.

clue.text: Pure heart possessed by beaten Masai warrior

indicators.note: possessed by means held inside the other letters
beaten suggests the letters of Masai are knocked out of shape
heart asks for the central letters of the word Pure

explanation.surface: A Masai fighter, defeated, keeps an innocent heart.
explanation.walkthrough: The Masai are themselves East African warriors, a neat decoy: 'beaten' jumbles the tribe's name and 'possessed by' tucks the heart of Pure inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A samurai was a member of Japan's hereditary warrior class.

clue.text: How doctors perform in the theatre?

definitions.text: How doctors perform in the theatre?

parts.words: How doctors perform in the theatre?
parts.note: theatre suggests a stage show but means the operating theatre, where surgeons work by cutting patients open

explanation.surface: A question about how medics act on stage.
explanation.definitionFit: Surgeons in an operating theatre act by carrying out surgery, so they work in that manner.

clue.text: A fascination with bank charges?

parts.note: read whimsically as a fascination (an interest) that scores or values (rates); straight it is what a bank charges for a loan

explanation.surface: Someone is oddly obsessed with what banks charge.
explanation.definitionFit: The percentages a lender charges on borrowed money are what banks bill customers.

clue.text: Plain dish with a bun in the middle

parts.note: a plate is a dish

indicators.note: in the middle asks for the centre letter of bun

explanation.surface: A simple plate with a bun placed at its centre.
explanation.definitionFit: A plateau is a raised area of level ground, a kind of plain.

clue.text: One in charge warning worker

parts.note: fore is the golfer's shouted warning
a man is a worker, as in a hired hand

explanation.surface: A supervisor cautions an employee.
explanation.definitionFit: A foreman is the person who supervises a group of workers.

clue.text: Full fare is halved — permitted during exercises

indicators.note: is halved keeps only the second half of the word fare
during means sitting inside the other letters

parts.note: PE is physical education, school exercises
to let is to permit

explanation.surface: A full meal is cut in half, allowed during gym class.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fare' looks like food here; 'is halved' keeps its back half, and 'during' sets the permission inside school exercises.
explanation.definitionFit: Replete means filled up, especially with food.

clue.text: Dream — always one welcomed by engineers

indicators.note: welcomed by means taken in between those letters

parts.note: RE is the Royal Engineers, a British army corps
ever means always
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A dream that engineers always welcome.
explanation.definitionFit: A reverie is a daydream, a state of pleasant musing.

clue.text: Trouble started with the next in line of them

indicators.note: started points to the opening letter of Trouble

parts.note: an heir is next in line to inherit

explanation.surface: Strife began with the successor to the throne.
explanation.definitionFit: Their is the possessive form meaning belonging to them.

clue.text: Supply weapons before cities arranged a truce

parts.note: to arm is to supply with weapons

indicators.note: arranged means the letters of cities are put into a fresh order

explanation.surface: Weapons are handed out before cities agree to a ceasefire.
explanation.definitionFit: An armistice is an agreement to stop fighting, a truce.

clue.text: Kills the people accepting a credit

indicators.note: accepting means the outer word takes the other letters inside

parts.note: the masses are the ordinary people
CR is the accounting abbreviation for credit

explanation.surface: The populace is accepting of a credit arrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: To massacre is to slaughter, so massacres is a strong word for kills.

clue.text: Man generally with right to enter queues making jokes

parts.note: one is the pronoun for a person in general

indicators.note: to enter means going inside the other word

parts.note: lines are queues

explanation.surface: People usually entitled to jump queues end up telling gags.
explanation.definitionFit: A one-liner is a short joke or quip delivered in a single sentence.

clue.text: Stores poem set to uplifting melody

indicators.note: set means the letters of poem are rearranged
in a down clue uplifting means the word reads from the bottom upwards

parts.note: an air is a melody

explanation.surface: A poem is set to an inspiring tune.
explanation.walkthrough: 'set' makes EMPO from POEM; 'uplifting' turns AIR into RIA.
explanation.definitionFit: Emporia, plural of emporium, are large shops or stores.

clue.text: Think of one periodical in English

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one
a mag is a magazine, a periodical

explanation.surface: Consider a magazine published in English.
explanation.definitionFit: To imagine something is to form it in the mind, to think of it.

clue.text: Influence dismissed by heartless colonel

indicators.note: heartless strips the word colonel to its first and last letters

parts.note: in cricket a dismissed batsman is out

explanation.surface: A colonel without compassion loses power.
explanation.definitionFit: Clout is informal for power or influence, especially political.

clue.text: Put up all art necessarily held to be fundamental

indicators.note: Put up says the hidden letters are read backwards
held says the letters are contained within the words all art necessarily

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: All art must be accepted as essential.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft took 'held' into the definition, leaving the hidden run without its signal; 'held' is that signal and 'to be' links. 'Put up' reads the run upwards in this down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Central means of chief importance, core or fundamental.

clue.text: Little-known people who left school with remedy

parts.note: OBs are old boys, former pupils of a school
a cure is a remedy

explanation.surface: Former pupils come with a treatment.
explanation.definitionFit: Obscure means not well known or not famous.

clue.text: Cheer very quietly during a double somersault

indicators.note: during means placed inside the other letters
somersault means the word is flipped over, read backwards

parts.note: dual means double
pp (pianissimo) is the musical mark for very quietly

explanation.surface: Someone praises an acrobat doing a quiet double flip.
explanation.walkthrough: PP is the musical marking pianissimo; 'somersault' flips the word for double over, and 'during' places the quiet marking inside.
explanation.definitionFit: To applaud is to clap or cheer in approval.

clue.text: Ring round for a music supplier

parts.note: a disc is a round flat object
O is ring-shaped

explanation.surface: Someone phones around looking for a musician.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ring round' suggests phoning people, but the two words give O and DISC, set down in answer order.
explanation.definitionFit: A disco is a party or club where recorded dance music is played.

clue.text: No memory for new names — one starts aging

indicators.note: new means the letters of names are made afresh

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

indicators.note: starts points to the first letter of aging

explanation.surface: Forgetting new names happens as a person starts getting old.
explanation.definitionFit: Amnesia is loss of memory.

clue.text: Stories about alternative river transport

indicators.note: about means the outer word goes around the other letters

parts.note: lies are stories, untruths
or introduces an alternative

explanation.surface: Tales about a different way of travelling by river.
explanation.definitionFit: Lorries are heavy goods vehicles used for road transport.

clue.text: Find another way for soldiers to beat fatigue at last

parts.note: RE, the Royal Engineers, are soldiers
to rout is to beat soundly

indicators.note: at last points to the final letter of fatigue

explanation.surface: Troops finally overcome exhaustion.
explanation.definitionFit: To reroute is to send by a different route.

clue.text: Young lady who produced German wine around the West of Innsbruck

parts.note: made means produced

indicators.note: around means the wine wraps the other letter

parts.note: Moselle is a wine from the Moselle valley in Germany

indicators.note: the West of a word is its leftmost, first letter

explanation.surface: A woman who made German wine near western Austria.
explanation.walkthrough: 'around' puts I (the West of Innsbruck) inside MOSELLE.
explanation.definitionFit: Mademoiselle is the French title for an unmarried or young woman.
